2008-140-anos-salva-de-prata.titulo: 140 years: a Silver Salver from the City Council
2008-140-anos-salva-de-prata.texto: At a solemn session proposed by councillor Jooji Hato, the São Paulo City Council presented América Lodge with a Silver Salver for its 140 years. The honour was received by José Luiz Carmanhães, Julio Chagas do Nascimento (Master of Honour) and Wagner Odri (Orator), among others.
2008-140-anos-salva-de-prata.contexto: The session recalled the founding of the Lodge by Law School students, the abolitionists who belonged to it and the creation, two years earlier, of the Instituto Herdeiros do Futuro.
detalhe: On 7 November 2008, at a solemn session in the chamber of the São Paulo City Council proposed by councillor Jooji Hato, the Lodge received a Silver Salver for its 140 years. Worshipful Master José Luis Carmanhães received the honour.

Also taking part for the Lodge were the Master of Honour Julio Chagas do Nascimento, after whom the Temple is named today, and the Orator Wagner Odri. Ricardo de Meo Fernandes represented Grand Master Benedito Marques Ballouk Filho, and Duarte Vaz Pacheco Castro Junior represented the national Grand Master Marcos José da Silva. Sante Fasanella Filho, Deputy Secretary for Social Assistance and Development, was also present.

In his speech, Carmanhães argued that the Lodge’s work must be made known in order to demystify Freemasonry. The Council’s report recalled the free schools of the nineteenth century, the province’s first public library and the Instituto Herdeiros do Futuro, which had already provided more than 800 consultations.

2018-150-anos-a-sessao-do.texto: On 09/11/2018 the Lodge celebrated 150 years since its founding with a session in its Temple, attended by the Most Serene Grand Master of the Grand Orient of São Paulo, Kamel Aref Saab. At the session the Treaty of Friendship between the GOSP and the Autonomous Supreme Conclave for the Brazilian Rite was signed, and the commemorative Sesquicentennial plaque was unveiled.
2018-150-anos-a-sessao-do.contexto: In 2018 América Lodge, one of the oldest in the State, completed a century and a half of activity, begun in 1868 by professors and students of the Law Academy of Largo de São Francisco.
detalhe: On 9 November 2018, exactly 150 years after its founding, the Lodge brought together Brethren, visitors and Masonic dignitaries in a commemorative session in its Temple, led by Worshipful Master Kiyoshi Tsumura. The Most Serene Grand Master of the Grand Orient of São Paulo, Kamel Aref Saab, and other GOSP dignitaries attended. According to the GOSP timeline, it was during this session that the Treaty of Friendship between the Grand Orient of São Paulo and the Autonomous Supreme Conclave for the Brazilian Rite was signed, a few weeks after the GOSP left the Grand Orient of Brazil. The emblems of the two Powers were displayed in the Temple, and gifts were exchanged, such as the GOSP’s standard and commemorative plate.

The same evening the Sesquicentennial plaque was unveiled, beneath the emblems of the GOSP and the Lodge and the seal “150 América 1868–2018”. The plaque bears a sentence from the Oração aos Moços (Address to the Young, 1920) by Rui Barbosa, initiated in the Lodge on 1 July 1869: “But if society cannot make equal those whom nature created unequal, each person, within the limits of their moral energy, can react against inborn inequalities through education, activity and perseverance...”. It also carries the motto: “May the Masons who pass through this Lodge take its past as inspiration and the future as a challenge.”
The celebrations also included the time capsule, sealed to be opened on 9 November 2068, and the tribute at the Lodge’s vault in the Consolação Cemetery (see the following items).

2018-gratidao-homenagem-no-jazigo-da.titulo: Gratitude: a tribute at the Lodge’s vault in Consolação
2018-gratidao-homenagem-no-jazigo-da.texto: As part of the 150th-anniversary celebrations, Brethren and their families visited the Consolação Cemetery, laid flowers at the Lodge’s vault and at Luiz Gama’s tomb, and fixed to the vault the “Gratitude” plaque, in memory of the Brethren who made the Lodge great.
2018-gratidao-homenagem-no-jazigo-da.contexto: Opened in 1858, the Consolação Cemetery was São Paulo’s first public cemetery and holds the tombs of central figures of São Paulo and Brazilian history, among them the abolitionist Luiz Gama.
detalhe: As part of the 150th-anniversary celebrations, Brethren of the Lodge and their families walked through the Consolação Cemetery. They laid wreaths at the vault of América Lodge, a black-granite structure with the columns J and B and the Square and Compasses on its triangular pediment, and at Luiz Gama’s tomb. A plaque with the 150-year seal was fixed to the vault: “Gratitude. The members of América Masonic Lodge, on the occasion of its 150th anniversary, record their eternal gratitude and pay tribute to the Brethren who now rest in the Eternal East and who once made our beloved Lodge great. São Paulo, 9 November 2018.”

The tribute revived an old tradition recorded in the archived minutes. According to a 1933 report, the Lodge bought its first grave in Consolação on 7 August 1872 (row 24, no. 32), where Brethren Mattheus Camodo (1872) and José Krisman (1875) were buried. At the end of the nineteenth century, part of the initiation fee went to the vault fund. In 1925 Worshipful Master João Gallo presented the plan for a 12-niche vault for the Brethren, and in 1960–61 the Lodge’s “triangle” plot was acquired. There rests, among others, Julio Chagas do Nascimento, Worshipful Master of Honour.

The tomb of Luiz Gama, who died on 24 August 1882, has a monument bearing the inscription “Fraternal Tribute of Lodge America”. In 1930, on the centenary of his birth, the Orator recalled that América had initiated him and raised his mausoleum. In 1958 the Lodge proposed a metal plaque for the tomb. In 1963 Bro∴ Oswaldo Melantonio organised a pilgrimage to the tombs of illustrious Brazilians. The 2018 route also passed other historic tombs, such as that of the Marchioness of Santos, who donated the land for the cemetery.

2018-a-capsula-do-tempo-para.titulo: The time capsule: for the Brethren of 2068
2018-a-capsula-do-tempo-para.texto: At the 150th anniversary, the Lodge’s Brethren of 2018 placed items in a time capsule, sealed under a granite lid, to be opened at the bicentenary, on 9 November 2068.
2018-a-capsula-do-tempo-para.contexto: Time capsules keep objects and messages from one generation for another. América’s was designed to span half a century, until the Lodge’s 200th anniversary.
detalhe: As part of the Sesquicentennial, all the Brethren on the 2018 roll placed items in a time capsule addressed to the Brethren who will be in the Lodge at its bicentenary. The capsule was sealed under a granite lid with a metal plate: “Open on 09.11.2068 – E∴ V∴ – From the Brethren of Lodge America of 2018 to the Brethren of Lodge America of 2068”.

The plate bears the emblems of the Lodge, of the Instituto Herdeiros do Futuro, of the Instituto Brasilista and the 150-year seal. The Brethren who made the deposits are those listed on the Sesquicentennial plaque: the officers under Worshipful Master Kiyoshi Tsumura, the members and the Past Masters.

2018-o-painel-das-realizacoes-da.titulo: The mural of the Lodge’s achievements
2018-o-painel-das-realizacoes-da.texto: A large mural painted at the Lodge tells in images the Lodge’s history and causes: abolition, the Republic, the press, education, technical training and the city of São Paulo, around the emblem of América.
2018-o-painel-das-realizacoes-da.contexto: The mural takes up the causes the Lodge itself names as its own: “We fought for the abolition of slavery and it came, we fought for the Republic and it arrived, we fought for free and accessible education and it was established, we fought for technical training and it changed our state.”
detalhe: The mural, hand-painted and framed on the staircase of the Lodge’s building, was recorded during the 150th-anniversary celebrations. It reads from left to right. It begins with the flag of São Paulo and the hands breaking their chains, symbol of abolition, beside the coat of arms of the Republic of 15 November 1889.

In the centre are the front pages of A Província de São Paulo, with the Proclamation of the Republic, and of O Estado de S. Paulo, a newspaper the Lodge counts among the institutions founded by its Brethren. The Lodge’s emblem, with the date 9 November 1868, is surrounded by medallions of the city: the Ibirapuera lake, the Sé Cathedral, the Altino Arantes Building, the cable-stayed bridge, the hand of the Latin America Memorial, the Copan, MASP, Luz Station, the Santa Ifigênia Viaduct and the Municipal Theatre.

On the right, over the flag of Brazil, two children study side by side, a reminder of the Lodge’s free schools. A young man works at a saw, an image of technical training. The mural is completed by the Monument to the Bandeiras and the Law School of Largo de São Francisco, birthplace of the Lodge’s founders.

2018-a-loja-america-segue-com.titulo: América Lodge stays with the GOSP
2018-a-loja-america-segue-com.texto: In the break between the Grand Orient of São Paulo and the Grand Orient of Brazil, América Lodge remained in the GOSP, which has since acted as an autonomous Masonic Power. The minutes of this period have not yet been added to the digital archive.
2018-a-loja-america-segue-com.contexto: It is not the first time the Lodge has lived through a separation between the two Powers. In 1921, when the GOSP was born, the Lodge split into two groups, one on each side; in 1972, in the Headquarters Building crisis, the minutes show the Lodge on the side of the GOB. In 2018 the GOSP contested the GOB’s national elections and approved in assembly, on 15/09/2018, its withdrawal from the federation; the lodges that wished to remain in the GOB organised themselves as the GOB-SP.

2019-diploma-de-reconhecimento-na-camara.titulo: Certificate of Recognition at the City Council
2019-diploma-de-reconhecimento-na-camara.texto: At the Solemn Session for Freemasons’ Day at the São Paulo City Council, which brought together Brethren of the GOSP, the GOP and the GLESP, América Lodge received the Certificate of Recognition for its members’ work in charity and in spreading good morals.
2019-diploma-de-reconhecimento-na-camara.contexto: Freemasons’ Day (20 August) recalls the 1822 session of the Grand Orient of Brazil linked to Independence.
detalhe: On the afternoon of 24 August 2019 the São Paulo City Council held, in the Noble Hall of the Anchieta Palace, a Solemn Session to celebrate Freemasons’ Day. Brethren of the State’s three Masonic Powers gathered: the Grand Orient of São Paulo, the Grande Oriente Paulista and the Grand Lodge of the State of São Paulo.

The session was convened by councillor Caio Miranda Carneiro, under the municipal law that includes Freemasons’ Day in the city calendar (Law No. 14,485/2007, Art. 7, item CLXIV), together with the National Institute for the Development of Municipalities (INADEM). Lodges of all the Powers were honoured.

The “Aug∴ Resp∴ Symbolic Lodge América No. 189”, under the jurisdiction of the Grand Orient of São Paulo, received the Certificate of Recognition, dated 20 August 2019, “for the significant work undertaken by its members to ‘make humanity happy’”, for the study of Masonic philosophy, the practice of charity and the spreading of good morals, contributing to the human and social development of the city and to building a more just and perfect society.

The chamber was packed with Brethren, families and guests, before the historic murals of the Anchieta Palace. The honour came in the year the Lodge passed from Worshipful Master Kiyoshi Tsumura (2017–2019) to Alvimar Sanches de Magalhães Júnior (2019–2021), eleven years after the Silver Salver received from the same Council for the Lodge’s 140 years.

2019-revalidacao-da-carta-patente-do.texto: América Lodge, with three other centenarian Lodges, repeated the historic act of 1921 by revalidating the Charter that created the Grand Orient of São Paulo, as recorded in the GOSP magazine No. 38. The exact date of the act is still to be confirmed.
2019-revalidacao-da-carta-patente-do.contexto: The GOSP was founded on 29/07/1921 by São Paulo Lodges that left the Grand Orient of Brazil; that year América itself was split between the two sides.
detalhe: In 1921 part of São Paulo’s Lodges left the Grand Orient of Brazil and founded the Grand Orient of the State of São Paulo. América itself split. The minutes of August 1921 show one faction, presided over by João Gallo, joining the new Grand Orient and keeping the Lodge’s name, while another, meeting at the home of Worshipful Master Acácio Garibaldi, remained loyal to the GOB. The by-laws approved on 10/08/1921 already declare the Lodge “subordinate to the Grand Orient of the State of S. Paulo”.

Almost a century later, América Lodge and three other centenarian Lodges repeated the historic act of 1921 and revalidated the Charter that created the GOSP. The act was the cover story of the GOSP magazine Luzes No. 38 in December 2019 (p. 16), and the Lodge publicised it in January 2020.

2019-ihf-lanca-curso-de-empregabilidade.titulo: IHF launches an employability course for women
2019-ihf-lanca-curso-de-empregabilidade.texto: The Instituto Herdeiros do Futuro started a free employability course for women, in partnership with the São Paulo City Department of Human Rights and Citizenship.
2019-ihf-lanca-curso-de-empregabilidade.contexto: Besides caring for child victims of violence, the IHF works with their families, seeking to break the cycle of violence through the mothers’ financial independence as well.
detalhe: On 24 September 2019 the Instituto Herdeiros do Futuro began its free Employability Course for Women, aimed at promoting autonomy and financial independence. The course was offered in partnership with the São Paulo City Department of Human Rights and Citizenship, at the Maria de Lourdes Rodrigues Women’s Reference Centre, near Capão Redondo metro station.
So that the mothers could take part, the institute organised activities for the children with a support team during the classes.

2020-cestas-basicas-na-pandemia.texto: With the covid-19 crisis, the Lodge and the Instituto Herdeiros do Futuro organised a campaign to donate food parcels to assisted families who had lost their income; in April 2020, 120 families were helped.
2020-cestas-basicas-na-pandemia.contexto: The isolation measures of 2020 immediately hit informal workers and low-income families on the outskirts of São Paulo.
detalhe: With the covid-19 pandemic, many families assisted by the Lodge and the Instituto Herdeiros do Futuro lost almost all their income. In April 2020 the Lodge launched a campaign to donate food parcels and helped 120 families that month. In May the goal was to keep supporting the same families. The campaign, run with the Instituto Herdeiros do Futuro, collected food parcels (R$ 65) and hygiene and cleaning kits (R$ 45), aiming to help 300 families a month.
The campaign took place under Worshipful Master Alvimar Sanches de Magalhães Júnior (2019–2021).
fotos: The campaign poster: food parcels and hygiene kits, with a goal of 300 families a month.

2020-medalha-jose-bonifacio-na-camara.titulo: José Bonifácio Medal at the City Council
2020-medalha-jose-bonifacio-na-camara.texto: On the Lodge’s 152nd anniversary, the São Paulo City Council honoured Masonic organisations with the José Bonifácio Medal. The Lodge recorded the honour, tagging the Instituto Herdeiros do Futuro and the GOSP.
2020-medalha-jose-bonifacio-na-camara.contexto: The José Bonifácio Medal, bearing the effigy of the Patriarch of Independence, is awarded by the São Paulo City Council. In 2020 the solemn session still took place under pandemic restrictions.
detalhe: On 9 November 2020, exactly 152 years after the Lodge’s founding, the São Paulo City Council held a solemn session to present the José Bonifácio Medal to Masonic organisations distinguished in philanthropy, as part of the Freemasons’ Day celebrations.

The Lodge publicised the honour on its social media, tagging the Instituto Herdeiros do Futuro and the Grand Orient of São Paulo. In the TV Câmara coverage, Bro∴ Wagner Ricardo Odri spoke, then GOSP secretary for Social Action and president of the IHF. The Lodge was led by Worshipful Master Alvimar Sanches de Magalhães Júnior (2019–2021).

2021-loja-maconica-america-vira-marca.titulo: “Loja Maçônica América” becomes a registered trademark
2021-loja-maconica-america-vira-marca.texto: The National Institute of Industrial Property (INPI) granted the Lodge registration of the word mark “Loja Maçônica América”, valid until 03/08/2031.
2021-loja-maconica-america-vira-marca.contexto: A trademark registered with the INPI guarantees exclusive use of the name throughout Brazil in the registered class. The registration lasts ten years and may be renewed for equal successive periods.
detalhe: The application was filed with the INPI on 7 October 2020, during the 2019–2021 term, and registration was granted on 3 August 2021, with the certificate digitally signed on 25 August. It is a word mark for goods and services, owned by Loja Maçônica América, CNPJ 61.365.334/0001-53, at Rua Apeninos, 515.

The registration is in class 45 of the Nice Classification, which covers, among other things, spiritual and philosophical guidance services and the organisation of meetings for social integration, provided as social assistance. It expires on 3 August 2031, when it may be renewed.

2021-ihf-abre-nova-unidade-no.titulo: IHF opens a new unit in Capão Redondo
2021-ihf-abre-nova-unidade-no.texto: The Instituto Herdeiros do Futuro opened a new unit in the South Zone, an SPVV (Protection Service for Victims of Violence) at Rua Miguel Gonçalves Correia, 128.
2021-ihf-abre-nova-unidade-no.contexto: The SPVVs are services of the municipal social protection network, run in partnership between the city government and civil society organisations such as the IHF.
detalhe: In September 2021 the IHF announced the opening of a new unit, a Protection Service for Victims of Domestic Violence in the Capão Redondo and Campo Limpo area, at Rua Miguel Gonçalves Correia, 128. The new unit’s technical team appeared together in the announcement photo.
Expansion continued in the following years: Santo Amaro (2023), Capela do Socorro (2025) and Parelheiros (2026).

2023-fundacao-do-scorb.texto: Eighteen Masons holding the 33rd degree of the Brazilian Rite, among them several Brethren of América Lodge, met in the office of the Grand Orient of São Paulo and founded the Supreme Council for the Brazilian Rite (SCORB), the first regular philosophical Power of the Rite based in São Paulo, housed at Rua Apeninos, 515, the Lodge’s own address. With SCORB, all the degrees from the 4th to the 33rd of the Rite came to be conferred in São Paulo.
2023-fundacao-do-scorb.contexto: The Brazilian Rite, created at the beginning of the twentieth century and revived in the 1960s, is the only Masonic rite born in the country. América Lodge adopted the Rite in 1968–1969, at its centenary.
detalhe: On 28 March 2023, eighteen Masons holding the 33rd degree of the Brazilian Rite met in the office of the Grand Orient of São Paulo and founded the Supreme Council for the Brazilian Rite (SCORB), the first regular Power of the Rite based in São Paulo. With it, all the degrees from the 4th to the 33rd came to be conferred in the State.

América Lodge, which has practised the Brazilian Rite since the late 1960s, played a central role in the founding. Among the founders are six Brethren who were or would be Worshipful Masters of the Lodge: Wagner Ricardo Odri (2011–2013), Mauro Tippi (2013–2015), Pascoal Nicola Giantomasi (2015–2017), Kiyoshi Tsumura (2017–2019), Paulo Luiz Maximiliano (then Worshipful Master, 2021–2023) and José Carlos Gomes de Oliveira (2025–2027). The founders Newton Anielo Paulilo and Vani Queiroz de Alvarenga were also members of the Lodge, according to the Sesquicentennial plaque (2018). Mauro Tippi was chosen as the first Sovereign Grand Primate. SCORB is based at Rua Apeninos, 515, the Lodge’s own address.

By its third anniversary, in March 2026, SCORB already had Philosophical Bodies in São Paulo, Minas Gerais and Bahia. The Sublime Chapter América No. 01, which works in the Lodge’s temple, was the first Chapter affiliated with the new Power.

The founders were Mauro Tippi, Kiyoshi Tsumura, Paulo Luiz Maximiliano, Flávio Azevedo Thomaz da Cruz, Pascoal Nicola Giantomasi, Vani Queiroz de Alvarenga, Wagner Ricardo Odri, Roberto Boin, Felippe Moyses Betti Neto, José Carlos Gomes de Oliveira, Denis Souza do Nascimento, Newton Anielo Paulilo, Sandro Luiz da Silva, Atílio Gerevini, Alberto Einstein Novais, José Roberto Nascimento Freitas, Clóves Plácido Barbosa and Luiz Carlos de Campos.

2023-ihf-faz-17-anos-e.titulo: IHF turns 17 and opens the Santo Amaro unit
2023-ihf-faz-17-anos-e.texto: In a single celebration, the Instituto Herdeiros do Futuro marked its 17th anniversary, launched its new visual identity and opened its fifth unit, the SPVV Santo Amaro.
2023-ihf-faz-17-anos-e.contexto: Santo Amaro was the district where the IHF began in 2006. The new unit brought an institute service back to the area.
detalhe: In August 2023 the IHF announced it was opening a new SPVV in the Santo Amaro district and asked for six laptops to be donated to equip the unit. The opening took place on 13 September, together with the institute’s 17th-anniversary celebration and the launch of its new visual identity, with the current logo.
The unit’s plaque was unveiled at the ceremony. In 2026 the SPVV Santo Amaro turned three.

2024-capitulo-america-no-01-o.titulo: América Chapter No. 01, the first of SCORB
2024-capitulo-america-no-01-o.texto: The Sublime Chapter América, installed a few years after the Lodge adopted the Brazilian Rite, became the first Chapter affiliated with SCORB and works in the Julio Chagas do Nascimento Temple.
2024-capitulo-america-no-01-o.contexto: In the Brazilian Rite, the Chapters confer the philosophical degrees that follow the Lodge’s three symbolic degrees. América Chapter No. 01 receives Brethren from América and from other Lodges of the Rite.
detalhe: According to SCORB, América Lodge adopted the Brazilian Rite in its centenary year and played an important part in the Rite’s expansion in São Paulo. The Sublime Chapter América was installed a few years later and, with the creation of SCORB, became the first Chapter affiliated with the new Power, as No. 01.

For two decades, from 1993 to 2013, the Chapter was led by the Pow∴ Bro∴ Heitor Genta, 33°, a former Worshipful Master of the Lodge. On 27 November 2013 the Chapter’s members dedicated to him a plaque of “Eternal Gratitude” for his dedication to the Chapter and to the Sovereign Supreme Conclave of the Brazilian Rite, signed by the Sovereign Grand Primate Nei Inocencio dos Santos.

The Chapter meets in the Lodge’s temple, where it holds initiations and advancements to the 4th to 18th degrees. On 24 September 2025, for example, it initiated four Brethren into the 14th Degree: Augusto Reis, Neemias Ramos, Rodrigo do Carmo and Wander Simões. The session was presided over by the Aterzata José Carlos Gomes, in the presence of the Grand Primate Mauro Tippi and of Brethren Paulo Maximiliano, Kiyoshi Tsumura, Pascoal Giantomasi and Newton Anielo.

2024-scorb-completa-um-ano-e.titulo: SCORB turns one and invests 12 Brethren in the 33rd Degree
2024-scorb-completa-um-ano-e.texto: The Supreme Council for the Brazilian Rite celebrated its first anniversary in Mogi das Cruzes, with initiations into the 22nd and 33rd Degrees and talks on the organisation of the Rite.
2024-scorb-completa-um-ano-e.contexto: In one year SCORB grew from 18 founders to a network of Philosophical Bodies in São Paulo, Minas Gerais and Bahia.
detalhe: On 23 March 2024 SCORB celebrated its first year in the Orient of Mogi das Cruzes. The opening was led by the Grand Primate Mauro Tippi, a former Worshipful Master of the Lodge, and by the Grand Master of the GOSP, Benedito Marques Ballouk Filho, an Honorary Member of América Lodge.

Twelve Brethren were invested in the 33rd Degree, the Rite’s highest. There were talks on the Grand Regency (Sandro Luiz), the Grand Instruction (Paulo Maximiliano), the Grand Oratory (Wagner Odri), the Grand Secretariat (Flávio da Cruz) and the Grand Treasury (Kiyoshi Tsumura). Delegations came from Avaré, Campinas, Feira de Santana, Franca, Mogi das Cruzes, Poá, Santos, São Paulo, Sorocaba and Ubá.

2024-ihf-faz-18-anos-e.titulo: IHF turns 18 and tells its story
2024-ihf-faz-18-anos-e.texto: For the 18th anniversary of the Instituto Herdeiros do Futuro, a series of videos told the organisation’s story, with president and founder Wagner Odri and treasurer Mauro Tippi, both former Worshipful Masters of the Lodge.
2024-ihf-faz-18-anos-e.contexto: Fundraising remained the institute’s greatest challenge: demand for care exceeds the monthly resources available.
detalhe: In August 2024 the IHF turned 18, or 6,574 days of work, and published a series of videos about its history. In the first, Wagner Odri, president and one of the founders, told how the institute was born.

In the next video, Mauro Tippi, the IHF’s treasurer for 12 years, spoke about the organisation’s greatest challenge, fundraising, which is needed to give children and families the best support and to pay the professionals fairly.

2025-ihf-inaugura-o-shopping-solidario.texto: The Instituto Herdeiros do Futuro opened the Shopping Solidário, a permanent charity shop of second-hand clothes, shoes and toys at affordable prices, whose income supports the institute.
2025-ihf-inaugura-o-shopping-solidario.contexto: Charity shops and thrift stores give social organisations an income of their own, while serving the community with low-priced goods.
detalhe: The permanent charity shop project was announced at the end of 2024. In January 2025 the IHF received the keys to the property and began preparing the space with the help of volunteers and donations.
The Shopping Solidário opened on 10 May 2025, with second-hand clothes, shoes and toys in good condition, sold at affordable prices.

2025-a-loja-em-festa-a.titulo: The Lodge celebrates: the Matrimonial Consecration of Fernando and Izabella
2025-a-loja-em-festa-a.texto: On 16/08/2025 the Lodge’s Temple opened to family and friends for the Solemn Session of Matrimonial Consecration of Bro∴ Fernando Piovesana and Izabella Patta Pereira Piovesana. The ceremony, under the auspices of the Grand Orient of São Paulo, gave Masonic recognition to a union already celebrated in civil law, with an arch of steel, an oath on the Volume of the Sacred Law and the consecration under the Worshipful Master’s Square.
2025-a-loja-em-festa-a.contexto: The Matrimonial Consecration is one of the few sessions in which the Lodge opens its Temple to non-Masons. It does not replace civil marriage: it confirms a union already celebrated before the law and welcomes the Brother’s wife as the Lodge’s “sister-in-law”. In this case, the ceremony itself introduced the guests to América’s history, from Luiz Gama and Rui Barbosa to the Instituto Herdeiros do Futuro.
detalhe: On 16 August 2025 the Julio Chagas do Nascimento Temple hosted the Solemn Session of Matrimonial Consecration of Bro∴ Fernando Piovesana, a member of the Lodge, and Izabella Patta Pereira Piovesana. The date was not chosen by chance: as the Orator recalled, it was exactly 25 years since, on 16 August 2000, the couple had started dating. After seven years together and fifteen years apart, the two met again and reaffirmed their “yes” under the aegis of the Lodge.

The family’s link with the Order goes back a long way. The Orator recalled that the groom’s father, the late Bro∴ Ciro Piovesana, was a devoted Mason, and that his sister-in-law Zetti Piovesana is an active member of the Order of the Eastern Star. Fernando was initiated in América itself in 2013, and Izabella had just been initiated into the Order of the Eastern Star.

The opening. The Masons entered the Temple in order of degree, from Entered Apprentices to Master Masons, the Lights and the dignitaries, and finally the Worshipful Master. Six Master Masons bearing swords formed the arch of steel for the guests’ entrance, and each lady received a red rosebud tied with a white ribbon. While the roses were handed out, the Senior Warden explained to the guests what Freemasonry is. The Junior Warden told the Lodge’s history: the republican and abolitionist founders, the popular schools open to the enslaved, the Jabaquara Quilombo, the 1932 Revolution, Brethren such as Luiz Gama and Rui Barbosa, and the founding of the Instituto Herdeiros do Futuro.

The Volume of the Sacred Law was opened at the Gospel of Matthew (19:5–6), under the Square and Compasses. After the invocation to the Great Architect of the Universe, the Worshipful Master cast incense on the brazier. The couple then entered under a new arch of steel and were led to the Altar of Consecration. The National Flag was brought in to the sound of the National Anthem.

The symbols. The Worshipful Master broke a crystal rod to show that a union can last forever if it is kept safe from brutality and violence. The Lights spoke of a Mason’s duties as husband and father, and the Senior Warden quoted the definition of family by Rui Barbosa, a Brother of the Lodge: “a living fabric of intertwined souls”. The seven-branched candlestick was lit and the couple, kneeling, swore love and fidelity on the Sacred Book. Then came the rose (love) and the lily (purity), the blue and white marital cord, the cup into which the groom poured wine and the bride added water, from which both drank, and the reading of the legend of the rings by Bro∴ Newton, before the children handed over the rings.

The consecration. Standing before the altar with heads bowed, the couple received the consecration. The Worshipful Master held over them the Square from his collar and confirmed the union “to the Glory of the Great Architect of the Universe” and under the auspices of the Grand Orient of São Paulo. The whole Lodge acknowledged the couple with the incessant battery, and the Lights struck their gavels. Izabella received the rose and the lily, and Fernando received the Certificate of Matrimonial Consecration, already signed by the witnesses.

The closing. The National Flag left to the sound of the Flag Anthem and the Volume of the Sacred Law was closed. The Temple was packed with Brethren, family and friends. The couple left the Temple under a final arch of steel and a shower of rose petals, and received congratulations in the social hall, among the portraits and relics of the Lodge’s history.

2025-simposio-do-rito-brasileiro-reune.titulo: Brazilian Rite Symposium brings together 100 Brethren
2025-simposio-do-rito-brasileiro-reune.texto: Some 100 Brethren from São Paulo and Minas Gerais took part in the Brazilian Rite Symposium at the GOSP Cultural Centre in Liberdade. The Grand Primate Mauro Tippi paid tribute to SCORB’s 18 founders.
2025-simposio-do-rito-brasileiro-reune.contexto: The Brazilian Rite, born in 1914 and restructured in 1968, is among the most widely practised rites in the country.
detalhe: On 23 August 2025 SCORB held the Brazilian Rite Symposium to deepen the study of the Rite’s history, philosophy and ritual practices. The opening was led by the Grand Master of the GOSP, Renato José Garcia de Almeida, and by the Grand Primate Mauro Tippi.

Tippi paid tribute to SCORB’s 18 founders, among them six former Worshipful Masters of América Lodge: “These founders worked and continue to work hard and constantly”. Also present were the Grand Master of the GOMAR, Pedro de Brito, and dignitaries of the GOSP, the Modern Rite and the AASR.
papeis: Grand Primate of SCORB; former Worshipful Master
fotos: Brethren at the Brazilian Rite Symposium, at the GOSP Cultural Centre.

2025-o-rito-brasileiro-apresentado-a.titulo: The Brazilian Rite presented to Masons from ten countries
2025-o-rito-brasileiro-apresentado-a.texto: At an online meeting of Tycho Brahe Lodge, SCORB Brethren presented the Brazilian Rite to Masons from more than ten countries, with a talk by Bro∴ Fernando Piovesana of América Lodge.
2025-o-rito-brasileiro-apresentado-a.contexto: Tycho Brahe Lodge, founded in Sweden and linked to the Grand Lodge of the Principality of Liechtenstein, meets virtually every fortnight and holds travelling in-person sessions.
detalhe: On 31 August 2025 the Brazilian Rite was the theme of the online meeting of Tycho Brahe Lodge, presided over by Worshipful Master Carl T. Ek. The main talk was given by Bro∴ Fernando Piovesana, of América Lodge No. 189.

SCORB was represented by the Grand Primate Mauro Tippi, the Grand Secretary Flávio da Cruz, the Grand Treasurer Kiyoshi Tsumura and councillors Antônio Vieira de Miranda and José Carlos Gomes. Present were the Grand Master of the Grand Lodge of the Principality of Liechtenstein, Savino Batanov, and Brethren from Belgium, Brazil, Bulgaria, Denmark, the USA, Finland, England, Liechtenstein, Norway and Sweden. The theme was proposed by Leandro Delamare, GOSP Grand Secretary for Foreign Relations.
fotos: The online meeting of Tycho Brahe Lodge, with Brethren from several countries.

2025-ihf-inaugura-sua-6a-unidade.titulo: IHF opens its 6th unit, in Capela do Socorro
2025-ihf-inaugura-sua-6a-unidade.texto: The Instituto Herdeiros do Futuro opened its sixth unit, a Social Protection Service for Child and Adolescent Victims of Violence in Capela do Socorro, for 80 users and their families.
2025-ihf-inaugura-sua-6a-unidade.contexto: Capela do Socorro, on the city’s far south side, is one of the areas with the greatest demand for child protection services.
detalhe: In September 2025 the IHF announced the opening of its sixth unit, the SPSCAVV Capela do Socorro, with a specialised technical team to care for 80 children and adolescents and their families.
In the comments, someone familiar with the work wrote: “Congratulations Wagner Odri on yet another unit”.
fotos: The announcement of the IHF’s sixth unit.

2025-157-anos-busto-e-comenda.titulo: 157 years: bust and Luiz Gama Medal
2025-157-anos-busto-e-comenda.texto: The Lodge celebrated 157 years with an evening dedicated to Luiz Gama, in the Julio Chagas do Nascimento Temple, with more than 200 people. A bust of Luiz Gama was unveiled in the temple’s atrium, and the Luiz Gama Medal was awarded to the researcher Lígia Fonseca Ferreira and the actor Deo Garcez.
2025-157-anos-busto-e-comenda.contexto: Luiz Gama (1830–1882), a former slave who became a lawyer and freed hundreds of people in the courts, was recognised as a lawyer by the Brazilian Bar Association (OAB) in 2015 and entered in the Book of Heroes and Heroines of the Fatherland in 2018.
detalhe: On 5 November 2025 the Lodge celebrated its 157 years with an evening dedicated to Luiz Gama, one of its first Worshipful Masters. The session, in the Julio Chagas do Nascimento Temple, was presided over by Worshipful Master José Carlos Gomes de Oliveira and brought together more than 200 people, among Masons, families and guests, as well as Masonic dignitaries and civil society leaders.

Prof. Dr. Lígia Fonseca Ferreira, the leading researcher of Luiz Gama’s life and work, gave a public lecture. Her thesis on Gama was defended at the Sorbonne Nouvelle University (Paris 3) in 2001. The actor Deo Garcez, who for more than ten years has played the abolitionist in the play “Luiz Gama: Uma Voz pela Liberdade” and portrayed him in the TV series “Nos Tempos do Imperador” (2021), gave a stage performance in character as Gama, moving through the Temple among those present.

Both received the Luiz Gama Medal, awarded to those who stand out in promoting equality, culture and humanitarian values. On the same evening the Lodge unveiled a bust of Luiz Gama, placed prominently in the Temple’s atrium.

2026-painel-quebrando-o-ciclo-contra.titulo: “Breaking the Cycle” panel against child abuse
2026-painel-quebrando-o-ciclo-contra.texto: On 13 May, the Lodge and the Instituto Herdeiros do Futuro held the panel “Breaking the Cycle”, on information as a tool in fighting child abuse. In March the Lodge had already held a solemn session for the International Day for the Elimination of Racial Discrimination.
2026-painel-quebrando-o-ciclo-contra.contexto: 18 May is Brazil’s National Day against the Abuse and Sexual Exploitation of Children and Adolescents.
detalhe: On 13 May 2026 the Lodge and the Instituto Herdeiros do Futuro held the panel “Breaking the Cycle – Information as a Tool in Fighting Child Abuse: Caring, Protecting and Reporting is a Collective Commitment”. The panel marked 18 May, the National Day against the Abuse and Sexual Exploitation of Children and Adolescents.

The meeting was led by the psychologists and social workers in charge of the IHF’s six units. They presented the institute’s work, spoke about violence against children and answered questions from the audience. The IHF then had more than 80,000 cases of care and about 60 staff, and it is still run voluntarily by the Lodge’s members.

The panel filled the Temple with Brethren, families and guests. Books and drawings lay on the table, and teaching materials and toys used in the care sessions were displayed in the centre of the Temple. Brethren of the Lodge also addressed the audience, and at the end the speakers received flowers.

2026-scorb-investe-17-irmaos-no.contexto: The 33rd Degree of the Brazilian Rite, “Servant of the Order, the Fatherland and Humanity”, is the Rite’s highest.

Representatives came from Campinas, Cerquilho, Mogi das Cruzes, Ribeirão Preto, São Paulo, Sorocaba, Ubatuba and Ubá.

The ceremony was presided over by the Grand Primate Mauro Tippi. José Luiz Carmanhães, Pedro de Brito, Wagner Chiodi and Wilson Concílio were installed as members of the Supreme Council. The Magna Reitoria was represented by Sandro Silva (Regent), Paulo Maximiliano (Instructor), Wagner Ricardo Odri (Orator), Flávio da Cruz (Secretary), Kiyoshi Tsumura (Treasurer) and Pascoal Giantomasi (Chancellor). 2026-mauro-tippi-apresenta-o-rito.titulo: Mauro Tippi presents the Brazilian Rite at the GOSP26 Congress
2026-mauro-tippi-apresenta-o-rito.texto: The GOSP26 Congress brought together more than 500 Brethren on 24 and 25 July 2026. There, the Grand Primate of SCORB and former Worshipful Master of the Lodge, Mauro Tippi, gave the lecture “The Philosophical Project of the Brazilian Rite”.
2026-mauro-tippi-apresenta-o-rito.contexto: GOSP26 discussed humanity’s challenges and the role of Freemasonry in the twenty-first century, with speakers from Denmark, Mexico, Liechtenstein and Brazil.
detalhe: The GOSP26 Congress began with its official opening on Friday 24 July 2026 at 7:30 pm, streamed live on TV GOSP. At the opening, the National Flag entered with a guard of honour of swords. The congress theme was “When Freemasonry speaks to the world – The Order facing humanity’s challenges”.

On 25 July 2026, in the GOSP auditorium in Liberdade, Mauro Tippi presented “The Philosophical Project of the Brazilian Rite”: “many of the things they describe have been supported by the Brazilian Rite since its founding”, he observed, about the international presentations.

The Grand Master of the GOSP, Renato José Garcia de Almeida, announced that one of the nine temples at the Grand Orient’s headquarters would be decorated for the Brazilian Rite. The Rite and SCORB were represented by, among others, Paulo Maximiliano and councillors Benedito Marques Ballouk Filho, José Carlos Gomes de Oliveira and Pedro de Brito.

In the lecture, Tippi went through the Rite’s degrees, such as those of the Excelso Alto Colégio, among them the 31st (Guardian of the Public Good) and the 32nd (Guardian of Civic Virtue). He closed with the phrase “The Brazilian Rite is the product of everyone’s doctrine, intelligence and wisdom”, and with the Rite described as anchored in classical tradition, adapted to the cosmic geometry of the South and driven by the Brazilian fraternal spirit.

2026-herdeiros-do-futuro-faz-20.titulo: Herdeiros do Futuro turns 20 and inaugurates the site of its new headquarters
2026-herdeiros-do-futuro-faz-20.texto: On 29/08/2026 the Instituto Herdeiros do Futuro, created by the Brethren of the Lodge, celebrated 20 years with a barbecue in Campo Limpo, on the plot where its new headquarters will be built.
2026-herdeiros-do-futuro-faz-20.contexto: In two decades, the institute born in the Lodge’s social hall has become a reference in caring for children and families affected by violence in the south of the city.
detalhe: On 29 August 2026 the Instituto Herdeiros do Futuro celebrated 20 years with a barbecue in Campo Limpo, in the south of São Paulo. The party also marked the inauguration of the plot where the new headquarters will be built, announced on a banner: “This will be the future IHF headquarters”.

The Brethren of the Lodge worked as volunteers at the party, in blue aprons bearing the IHF brand and the Lodge’s emblems. On the stage they gathered with the institute’s staff and guests. There were speeches and moving moments, and a samba circle livened up the afternoon. Guests wore a wristband commemorating the 20 years.

In two decades the institute has provided psychosocial support to more than 80,000 children and adolescent victims of domestic violence. Today it runs six units and provides about 3,000 sessions of care a month. It has managed more than R$ 40 million in public and private funds, applied entirely to the cause. The Lodge saluted the Brethren who conceived and maintain the IHF, among them the founders of 2006, as well as its staff, professionals and partners.

2026-hoje-rua-apeninos-515.texto: According to the survey of the Lodge’s seats, América Lodge now meets at Rua Apeninos, 515, the address given on an INPI certificate. 2026-ihf-abre-o-spvv-parelheiros.texto: The Instituto Herdeiros do Futuro opened recruitment for the team of its new unit, the SPVV Parelheiros, on the far south side of São Paulo.
2026-ihf-abre-o-spvv-parelheiros.contexto: Parelheiros, on the far south side, is one of the city’s most vulnerable areas.

2026-homenagem-a-wagner-odri-pela.titulo: Tribute to Wagner Odri for the lecture “The history of América Lodge”
2026-homenagem-a-wagner-odri-pela.texto: At a session of the Lodge, Bro∴ Wagner Odri received an honorary plaque in recognition of the lecture “The history of América Lodge”, which he gave at Cidade Paulistana Lodge No. 7037.
2026-homenagem-a-wagner-odri-pela.contexto: Since 2026 the Lodge’s historical collection, with the minutes from 1874 onwards, has been transcribed and gathered in this portal.

On 4 November 2026, at a session of the Lodge in the Julio Chagas do Nascimento Temple presided over by Worshipful Master José Carlos Gomes de Oliveira, Odri received the honorary plaque from GOSP Coordinator João Luiz Amaral Júnior, a member of Cidade Paulistana Lodge.

2026-158-anos-a-loja-ganha.titulo: 158 years: the Lodge receives its memory portal
2026-158-anos-a-loja-ganha.texto: On the Lodge’s 158th anniversary, Bro∴ Fernando Piovesana, Treasurer, offered this portal to the Brethren as a gift: the history of América told through its own minutes, from 1874 to the present day, side by side with the history of Brazil and the world.
2026-158-anos-a-loja-ganha.contexto: Digital archives and memory projects have allowed century-old institutions to open collections once kept in cupboards and fragile books. In América’s case, the handwritten minutes survived changes of seat, splits and more than a century and a half of use.
detalhe: The starting point was the scans of the Lodge’s minute books: 3,687 handwritten pages, from 1874 to 1975. Each set of minutes was identified and gathered in an index of 2,417 sessions, with the date, type of session, who presided, venue, topics and a summary. The index gave rise to the Members’ Roll, with 2,258 names of Brethren, candidates and visitors mentioned over a century.

The minutes are also being transcribed word for word, on the Lodge’s letterhead and with a facsimile of each page. By this anniversary, 1,373 sets of minutes, from 1874 to 1942, could already be read in the portal beside the original manuscript; the rest are still being transcribed.

The work was carried out by Bro∴ Fernando Piovesana with the support of artificial intelligence (Claude, by Anthropic), which read the manuscripts, organised the index, cross-checked the information and drafted the texts, always checked by the Brother. Dates and names were compared with the minutes, the plaque of Worshipful Masters and the Lodge’s website and social media; where sources disagree, the portal records the disagreement rather than choosing one version.

Besides the minutes, the portal brings together more than one hundred landmarks in the Lodge’s history, the seats it has occupied, the gallery of Worshipful Masters, the administration and photographs of recent events, in Portuguese, Spanish and English. It can be viewed on a computer, on a phone or on a kiosk in the Lodge itself.

The portal remains open to contributions from the Brethren: photos, documents, invitations, diplomas and memories from any period can be sent through the Archive form, and each item is reviewed before it enters the timeline.
papeis: Treasurer; conceived and organised the portal

2026-homenagem-do-gosp-aos-158.titulo: GOSP tribute to the Lodge’s 158 years
2026-homenagem-do-gosp-aos-158.texto: On the Lodge’s 158th anniversary, the Grand Orient of São Paulo paid tribute to América with a commemorative piece that hails it as “Primate of the Brazilian Rite” and reproduces an excerpt from the speech of Bro∴ Amadeu Amaral at the Lodge’s 53rd anniversary, in 1921.
2026-homenagem-do-gosp-aos-158.contexto: The Grand Orient of São Paulo was founded on 29 July 1921 under the leadership of Brethren of América; the solemn session of 9 November that year, at which Amadeu Amaral spoke, was the first anniversary of the Lodge celebrated under the new Grand Lodge.
detalhe: The piece bears the seals of the Grand Orient of São Paulo (29 July 1921) and of the Lodge (9 November 1868) and the inscription “América Lodge – Primate of the Brazilian Rite – 158 Years”.

The chosen text is an excerpt from the speech of Bro∴ Amadeu Amaral, Orator of the Lodge and member of the Brazilian Academy of Letters, at the session of 9 November 1921: “‘América Lodge’, daughter of Américo, the good and great Américo de Campos […] ‘América Lodge’, an army in permanent struggle against every form of slavery […] Your name is a whole past of glories! Your name is the whole daring dream of a better humanity blossoming on the continent of peace and liberty!”

According to the minutes of that solemn session, presided over by Deputy Grand Master Col. Graça Martins, Amadeu Amaral gave a lecture on the past and present of the Lodge and took the oath as an affiliated member. In June 1922, the Lodge recorded the delivery of copies of the speech in Argentina.
papeis: Orator of the Lodge (1921); author of the quoted speech

1868|Segundo Reinado.texto: Brazil is an empire ruled by Emperor Pedro II, with an economy based on coffee exports and enslaved labour. The Paraguayan War (1864–1870) strengthens the Army and opens room for criticism of the monarchy. Gradual laws such as the Free Womb Law and the Sexagenarian Law prepare the Abolition of slavery, won in 1888 under strong popular pressure. In São Paulo, coffee advances across the west of the province, railways multiply and the first large waves of European immigrants arrive. It is also the time of the Religious Question, when Freemasonry clashes with bishops of the Catholic Church.

1889|Primeira República.texto: Proclaimed in 1889, the Republic adopts federalism and separates Church and State. Power is concentrated in the state oligarchies, above all those of São Paulo and Minas Gerais, in the so-called “coffee with milk” politics. The city of São Paulo grows at a fast pace with coffee, immigration and the first industries, becoming a large urban and working-class centre. The period is marked by revolts (Canudos, the Vaccine Revolt, the Revolt of the Lash, tenentismo) and by the Modern Art Week of 1922, and it ends with the 1929 crisis, which brings down coffee prices.

1930|Era Vargas: Governo Provisório e Co.nome: Vargas Era: Provisional and Constitutional Government
1930|Era Vargas: Governo Provisório e Co.texto: The Revolution of 1930 brings Getúlio Vargas to power and ends the hegemony of the São Paulo and Minas Gerais oligarchies. São Paulo reacts with the Constitutionalist Revolution of 1932 and, although defeated militarily, sees the country gain a new Constitution in 1934. The government centralises power, creates labour laws and introduces the secret ballot and women’s suffrage. In the city of São Paulo the University of São Paulo is founded (1934), amid sharp polarisation between communists and integralists.

1937|Estado Novo.texto: With the coup of 10 November 1937, Vargas closes Congress, dissolves the parties and rules as a dictator, with censorship and political police. The State drives heavy industry, creates the minimum wage and gathers the labour laws in the CLT. In Europe, authoritarian regimes persecute Freemasonry, and the Second World War leads Brazil to fight alongside the Allies in Italy. The contradiction between fighting dictatorships abroad and keeping one at home contributes to the fall of Vargas in 1945.

1945|República de 1946.texto: Under the 1946 Constitution the country lives through almost two decades of elections, national parties and intense political life. It is the era of national developmentalism: Petrobras, the car industry, Juscelino Kubitschek’s Targets Plan and the building of Brasília. São Paulo becomes Brazil’s largest city and industrial centre, with large migration from the Northeast and cultural ferment (MASP, the Biennial, television). The period ends amid the Cold War, high inflation and the political crisis of the João Goulart government.

1964|Regime militar.texto: The 1964 coup installs a regime in which generals succeed one another in the Presidency, with indirect elections, a two-party system and institutional acts. Institutional Act No. 5 of 1968 widens censorship and repression, while the “economic miracle” brings fast growth and rising inequality. From 1974 a “slow, gradual and safe” opening begins, accelerated by the economic crisis, the strikes in São Paulo’s ABC region and the Amnesty Law of 1979. The Diretas Já campaign (1984) mobilises millions, and the regime ends with the indirect election of Tancredo Neves.

1985|Nova República.texto: Redemocratisation culminates in the 1988 Constitution, which expands rights and restores direct presidential elections. After years of hyperinflation, the Real Plan (1994) stabilises the currency. The country goes through changes of government, two impeachments (1992 and 2016), major sporting events and economic and health crises such as the covid-19 pandemic. São Paulo consolidates itself as a global metropolis and the country’s financial, services and cultural centre.

1868|Fundada a Companhia Paulista de Est.texto: Coffee planters create the Companhia Paulista to take rails into the interior, linking the plantations to the port of Santos via the São Paulo Railway.

1868|Restauração Meiji no Japão.texto: Imperial power is restored in Japan, which begins a rapid modernisation inspired by the West.

1868|Queda do gabinete Zacarias.texto: Pedro II replaces the Liberal cabinet with a Conservative one lacking support in the Chamber. The crisis radicalises the Liberals and helps give rise to the republican movement.

1869|Inaugurado o Canal de Suez.texto: The canal links the Mediterranean to the Red Sea and drastically shortens routes between Europe and Asia.

1870|Fim da Guerra do Paraguai.texto: The death of Solano López at Cerro Corá ends the bloodiest conflict in South American history.

1870|Publicado o Manifesto Republicano.texto: In Rio de Janeiro, the newspaper A República publishes the manifesto that gives rise to the Republican Party.

1871|Unificação da Alemanha.texto: After defeating France, Prussia proclaims the German Empire at Versailles.

1871|Lei do Ventre Livre.texto: Declares free the children of enslaved women born from that date on, under the cabinet of the Viscount of Rio Branco.

1872|Começa a Questão Religiosa.texto: A priest is punished by the bishop of Rio for speaking at a Masonic lodge; the bishops of Olinda and Pará begin to ban brotherhoods with Masons.

1873|Convenção de Itu.texto: Coffee planters and professionals meeting in Itu found the São Paulo Republican Party (PRP).

1874|Bispos condenados à prisão.texto: Dom Vital (Olinda) and Dom Macedo Costa (Pará) are sentenced by the Supreme Court of Justice for disobeying the imperial government.

1875|Nasce A Província de São Paulo.titulo: A Província de São Paulo is born
1875|Nasce A Província de São Paulo.texto: First issue of the newspaper linked to the republicans, which after the Republic would be renamed O Estado de S. Paulo.

1875|Anistia encerra a Questão Religiosa.texto: The government pardons the imprisoned bishops, ending the conflict that had strained relations between the Monarchy and the Church.

1877|Grande Oriente de França muda seus.titulo: Grand Orient of France changes its principles
1877|Grande Oriente de França muda seus.texto: The GOF stops requiring belief in God, leading to a break with English Freemasonry and a lasting division between Masonic currents.

1877|Grande Seca no Nordeste.texto: The drought of 1877–1879 kills hundreds of thousands and causes large-scale migration from the Northeast.

1880|Abolicionismo ganha força.texto: Joaquim Nabuco and others found the Brazilian Anti-Slavery Society; the movement spreads through newspapers, clubs and the streets.

1881|Lei Saraiva.texto: An electoral reform introduces direct voting but requires income and, later, literacy, greatly restricting the number of voters.

1883|Reunificação do Grande Oriente do B.texto: The Grand Orients of Lavradio and of the Beneditinos, separated since 1863, once again form a single Masonic Power.

1884|Conferência de Berlim.texto: European powers set the rules for the colonial partition of Africa (1884–1885).

1884|Ceará abole a escravidão.texto: Ceará becomes the first province to free all enslaved people, four years before the Golden Law.

1885|Lei dos Sexagenários.texto: Frees enslaved people over 60, a measure abolitionists considered timid.

1887|Hospedaria de Imigrantes do Brás.texto: The hostel that received millions of immigrants on their way to the coffee farms opens; today it houses the Immigration Museum.

1888|Lei Áurea.texto: Princess Isabel signs the law that abolishes slavery in Brazil, the last country in the Americas to do so.

1889|Torre Eiffel e Exposição de Paris.titulo: Eiffel Tower and the Paris Exposition
1889|Torre Eiffel e Exposição de Paris.texto: The Universal Exposition celebrates the centenary of the French Revolution and presents the Eiffel Tower.

1889|Proclamação da República.texto: A military movement led by Deodoro da Fonseca overthrows the Monarchy; the imperial family leaves for exile.

1890|Deodoro, grão-mestre do GOB.titulo: Deodoro, Grand Master of the GOB
1890|Deodoro, grão-mestre do GOB.texto: The first President of the Republic also takes on the Grand Mastership of the Grand Orient of Brazil, a sign of the weight of Freemasonry among the republicans.

1890|Separação entre Igreja e Estado.texto: A decree of the Provisional Government ends Catholicism as the official religion and guarantees freedom of worship.

1891|Primeira Constituição republicana.texto: Establishes federalism, presidentialism and direct voting for literate men.

1891|Inaugurada a Avenida Paulista.texto: Laid out along the high ridge, the avenue becomes the address of the coffee barons’ mansions.

1892|Inaugurado o Viaduto do Chá.texto: The crossing over the Anhangabaú Valley drives the city’s expansion beyond the old centre.

1893|Revolta da Armada e Revolução Feder.texto: Floriano faces a rebellion by part of the Navy in Rio and a civil war in the South (1893–1895).

1893|Criada a Escola Politécnica.texto: The engineering school trains technicians for São Paulo’s railways, public works and industries; it would later become part of USP.

1894|Prudente de Morais, primeiro presid.titulo: Prudente de Morais, first civilian president
1894|Prudente de Morais, primeiro presid.texto: The São Paulo politician takes office, beginning the dominance of the civilian oligarchies.

1897|Destruição de Canudos.texto: After four military expeditions, the settlement led by Antônio Conselheiro in the backlands of Bahia is razed.

1898|Política dos governadores.texto: Campos Sales seals an agreement of mutual support between the federal government and the state oligarchies.

1900|Primeiro bonde elétrico.texto: The Light company inaugurates the electric tram in the capital, a symbol of the city’s modernisation.

1901|Nova Estação da Luz.texto: Built with a structure brought from England, the station becomes the city’s main gateway.

1903|Tratado de Petrópolis.texto: Negotiated by the Baron of Rio Branco, it incorporates Acre into Brazil in exchange for compensation to Bolivia.

1904|Revolta da Vacina.texto: Rio’s population rebels against compulsory vaccination and authoritarian urban reforms.

1906|Convênio de Taubaté.texto: São Paulo, Minas Gerais and Rio agree to buy surplus coffee to support its international price.

1906|Voo do 14-Bis em Paris.texto: Santos-Dumont flies a heavier-than-air machine before witnesses.

1908|Chegada do Kasato Maru.texto: The ship lands in Santos the first Japanese immigrants hired for the coffee farms.

1910|República em Portugal.texto: A revolution overthrows the Portuguese monarchy.

1910|Revolta da Chibata.texto: Sailors led by João Cândido rebel against corporal punishment in the Navy.

1911|Theatro Municipal de São Paulo.texto: The theatre opens, becoming a symbol of coffee wealth and the stage of the 1922 Modern Art Week.

1912|Guerra do Contestado.texto: Conflict between peasants and government forces in Santa Catarina and Paraná (1912–1916).

1914|Começa a Primeira Guerra Mundial.texto: Austria-Hungary declares war on Serbia, and the conflict soon draws in the great European powers.

1917|Greve Geral de 1917.texto: In July, workers halt São Paulo’s factories for better wages and working conditions.

1917|Brasil entra na Primeira Guerra.titulo: Brazil enters the First World War
1917|Brasil entra na Primeira Guerra.texto: After Brazilian ships are sunk, the country declares war on Germany.

1917|Revolução Russa.texto: The Bolsheviks, led by Lenin, take power in Russia.

1918|Gripe espanhola.texto: The pandemic kills tens of thousands in Brazil, among them President-elect Rodrigues Alves (1919).

1918|Fim da Primeira Guerra Mundial.titulo: End of the First World War
1918|Fim da Primeira Guerra Mundial.texto: The armistice ends the fighting in Europe.

1919|Tratado de Versalhes.texto: Imposes harsh conditions on defeated Germany and creates the League of Nations.

1921|Fundação do Grande Oriente de São P.titulo: Founding of the Grand Orient of São Paulo
1921|Fundação do Grande Oriente de São P.texto: São Paulo lodges meeting on Rua Tabatinguera found the Grand Orient of São Paulo (GOSP), separating from the Grand Orient of Brazil.

1922|Semana de Arte Moderna.texto: At the Municipal Theatre, artists such as Mário de Andrade and Anita Malfatti launch Brazilian modernism.

1922|Fundado o Partido Comunista.texto: The PCB is created in Niterói; it would spend most of the century outlawed.

1922|Revolta dos 18 do Forte.titulo: Revolt of the 18 of the Fort
1922|Revolta dos 18 do Forte.texto: Young officers rebel at Copacabana Fort, starting the tenentista movement.

1922|Centenário da Independência.texto: A large international exhibition in Rio celebrates the hundred years; the country’s first radio broadcast takes place.

1922|Marcha sobre Roma.texto: Mussolini comes to power in Italy, beginning the fascist regime.

1924|Revolta Paulista de 1924.texto: Rebel lieutenants occupy the capital for about three weeks; the city is bombarded by the federal government.

1925|Coluna Prestes.texto: Tenentista rebels travel some 25,000 km through Brazil’s interior (1925–1927).

1925|Fascismo proíbe a maçonaria.texto: The Mussolini regime’s law on associations leads to the closing of Masonic lodges in Italy.

1927|Surgem as Grandes Lojas estaduais.texto: A split in the Grand Orient of Brazil gives rise to the Grand Lodges, the second major branch of Brazilian Freemasonry.

1927|Lojas do GOSP fundam a Grande Loja.titulo: GOSP lodges found the Grand Lodge of the State of São Paulo
1927|Lojas do GOSP fundam a Grande Loja.texto: Lodges linked to the Grand Orient of São Paulo found the Grand Lodge of the State of São Paulo (GLESP), another São Paulo Masonic Power.

1929|Concluído o Edifício Martinelli.texto: The city’s first skyscraper, a symbol of its vertical growth and of immigrant wealth.

1929|O GOSP se filia ao Grande Oriente d.titulo: GOSP joins the Grand Orient of Brazil
1929|O GOSP se filia ao Grande Oriente d.texto: Eight years after the separation, the Grand Orient of São Paulo rejoins the GOB as a federated state Grand Orient.

1929|Quebra da Bolsa de Nova York.texto: “Black Thursday” begins the Great Depression, which brings down coffee prices and shakes São Paulo.

1930|Revolução de 1930.texto: An armed movement brings Getúlio Vargas to power and ends the First Republic.

1932|Código Eleitoral e voto feminino.texto: Creates the Electoral Court and the secret ballot and guarantees women the right to vote.

1932|Morte de Martins, Miragaia, Dráusio.titulo: Death of Martins, Miragaia, Dráusio and Camargo
1932|Morte de Martins, Miragaia, Dráusio.texto: Young men killed in a protest against Vargas give their initials to the MMDC, symbol of the São Paulo movement.

1932|Revolução Constitucionalista.texto: São Paulo takes up arms against the Vargas government demanding a Constitution; the fight lasts almost three months.

1933|Hitler chega ao poder.texto: Appointed Chancellor of Germany, Hitler quickly installs the Nazi dictatorship.

1934|Fundação da USP.texto: The São Paulo government creates the University of São Paulo, with professors brought from Europe.

1934|Constituição de 1934.texto: Incorporates labour rights and women’s suffrage; Vargas is elected president by the Assembly.

1935|Departamento de Cultura de São Paul.texto: Under Mário de Andrade, the city creates children’s parks, libraries and research on popular culture.

1935|Salazar dissolve as sociedades secr.texto: A Portuguese law of 1935 strikes the Grand Orient Lusitano, which goes underground.

1935|Nazismo dissolve as lojas na Aleman.titulo: Nazism dissolves the lodges in Germany
1935|Nazismo dissolve as lojas na Aleman.texto: The last German Masonic lodges are abolished; Masons are persecuted throughout the occupied territory.

1935|Levante comunista de 1935.texto: A revolt in barracks in Natal, Recife and Rio is defeated and serves as a pretext to harden the regime.

1936|Guerra Civil Espanhola.texto: The military uprising led by Franco opens a war that ends with the Franco dictatorship in 1939.

1937|Golpe do Estado Novo.texto: Vargas closes Congress, imposes a new Constitution and rules as a dictator.

1940|Franco pune a maçonaria na Espanha.texto: A law repressing Freemasonry and communism leads to the imprisonment and exile of thousands of Spanish Masons.

1940|Inaugurado o Estádio do Pacaembu.texto: The municipal stadium becomes a symbol of São Paulo football.

1940|Criado o salário mínimo.texto: Vargas introduces a national minimum wage.

1941|Criada a Companhia Siderúrgica Naci.texto: The Volta Redonda mill marks the beginning of heavy industry in the country.

1942|Brasil declara guerra ao Eixo.titulo: Brazil declares war on the Axis
1942|Brasil declara guerra ao Eixo.texto: After Brazilian merchant ships are sunk by German submarines.

1943|Consolidação das Leis do Trabalho.texto: The CLT brings together Brazil’s labour laws.

1945|Tomada de Monte Castello.texto: The best-remembered victory of the Brazilian Expeditionary Force in the Italian campaign.

1945|Fim da guerra na Europa.titulo: End of the war in Europe

1945|Bomba atômica em Hiroshima.texto: The USA uses the atomic weapon for the first time; Japan would surrender weeks later.

1945|Criada a ONU.texto: The Charter of the United Nations comes into force.

1945|Deposição de Vargas.texto: The military remove Vargas and end the Estado Novo; elections are held in December.

1946|Constituição de 1946.texto: Restores democracy, the independence of the branches of government and individual freedoms.

1947|Começa a Guerra Fria.texto: The Truman Doctrine marks the rivalry between the USA and the Soviet Union; Brazil breaks off relations with the USSR and revokes the PCB’s registration.

1947|Fundado o MASP.texto: Assis Chateaubriand and Pietro Maria Bardi create the São Paulo Museum of Art.

1948|Declaração Universal dos Direitos H.texto: Adopted by the UN General Assembly in Paris.

1949|Revolução Chinesa.texto: Mao Zedong proclaims the People’s Republic of China.

1950|Maracanazo.texto: Uruguay beats Brazil at the Maracanã and wins the World Cup held in Brazil.

1950|Primeira transmissão de TV.texto: Assis Chateaubriand’s TV Tupi inaugurates television in Brazil, in São Paulo.

1951|Primeira Bienal de São Paulo.texto: The international exhibition puts the city on the world circuit of modern art.

1953|Greve dos 300 mil.texto: A large stoppage by São Paulo workers against the high cost of living.

1953|Criação da Petrobras.texto: A law establishes the state oil monopoly after the campaign “The oil is ours”.

1954|IV Centenário de São Paulo.texto: The city celebrates 400 years; Ibirapuera Park, designed with Oscar Niemeyer, is the great work of the festivities.

1954|Suicídio de Getúlio Vargas.texto: Amid a serious political crisis, Vargas kills himself in the Catete Palace and leaves a testament letter.

1956|Posse de Juscelino Kubitschek.texto: JK launches the Targets Plan, “50 years in 5”; car makers settle in São Paulo’s ABC region.

1958|Brasil campeão mundial na Suécia.texto: With Pelé and Garrincha, the national team wins its first World Cup; the same year bossa nova emerges.

1959|Revolução Cubana.texto: Guerrillas led by Fidel Castro overthrow the dictator Fulgencio Batista.

1960|São Paulo, maior cidade do país.titulo: São Paulo, the country’s largest city
1960|São Paulo, maior cidade do país.texto: The 1960 census shows the city of São Paulo overtaking Rio de Janeiro in population.

1960|Inauguração de Brasília.texto: The federal capital moves from Rio de Janeiro to the Central Plateau.

1961|Construção do Muro de Berlim.texto: East Germany divides the city, the greatest symbol of the Cold War.

1961|Renúncia de Jânio Quadros.texto: João Goulart is only allowed to take office with the adoption of a parliamentary system.

1962|Crise dos Mísseis em Cuba.texto: In October, the USA and the USSR come to the brink of nuclear war.

1964|Marcha da Família com Deus pela Lib.titulo: March of the Family with God for Freedom
1964|Marcha da Família com Deus pela Lib.texto: A large demonstration in central São Paulo against the Goulart government.

1964|Golpe militar.texto: The military depose João Goulart; the regime that would rule the country for 21 years begins.

1965|AI-2 e o bipartidarismo.texto: Abolishes the parties and makes the presidential election indirect; ARENA and the MDB are created.

1968|Maio de 68 e Primavera de Praga.texto: Student protests in France and the Soviet invasion of Czechoslovakia mark a year of rebellion.

1968|Passeata dos Cem Mil.titulo: March of the One Hundred Thousand
1968|Passeata dos Cem Mil.texto: Students, artists and religious figures protest against the regime in Rio de Janeiro.

1968|Batalha da Rua Maria Antônia.texto: A clash between students of USP and Mackenzie in the city centre.

1968|Ato Institucional nº 5.texto: Closes Congress, suspends habeas corpus for political crimes and widens censorship.

1969|Homem chega à Lua.texto: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walk on the Moon on the Apollo 11 mission.

1970|Tricampeonato mundial no México.texto: Pelé’s team wins the World Cup at the height of the “economic miracle”.

1973|Cisão no Grande Oriente do Brasil.titulo: Split in the Grand Orient of Brazil
1973|Cisão no Grande Oriente do Brasil.texto: State Grand Orients break with the GOB and form a new branch, later gathered in COMAB.

1973|Primeiro choque do petróleo.texto: Arab countries raise oil prices, ending the cycle of fast growth in Brazil.

1973|O GOSP se desliga do Grande Oriente.titulo: GOSP leaves the Grand Orient of Brazil
1973|O GOSP se desliga do Grande Oriente.texto: The Grand Orient of São Paulo disaffiliates from the GOB. América’s minutes of 1972 already record circulars from the Central Power against the São Paulo Grand Mastership.

1973|Golpe no Chile.texto: The military led by Augusto Pinochet overthrow President Salvador Allende.

1974|Incêndio do Edifício Joelma.texto: One of the city’s worst urban tragedies, with almost 200 dead, changes safety regulations.

1974|Geisel e a abertura política.texto: President Ernesto Geisel announces a “slow, gradual and safe” easing.

1974|Revolução dos Cravos.texto: The military overthrow the dictatorship in Portugal; the African colonies become independent in 1975.

1974|Metrô de São Paulo.texto: Commercial operation of the first stretch begins, between Jabaquara and Vila Mariana.

1975|Fim da Guerra do Vietnã.texto: The fall of Saigon ends the war and leads to the country’s reunification.

1975|Morte de Vladimir Herzog.texto: The journalist dies in the custody of the DOI-Codi in São Paulo; the ecumenical service at the Cathedral becomes a landmark of resistance.

1978|Greves do ABC.texto: Metalworkers in São Paulo’s ABC region halt the factories, the first major strikes since 1968.

1979|Revolução Iraniana.texto: With the Shah overthrown, an Islamic republic is established; the second oil shock follows.

1979|Lei da Anistia.texto: Allows exiles to return and political prisoners to be freed; it also benefits agents of the State.

1980|O GOSP volta ao Grande Oriente do B.titulo: GOSP returns to the Grand Orient of Brazil
1980|O GOSP volta ao Grande Oriente do B.texto: The Grand Orient of São Paulo rejoins the GOB federation.

1980|Fundação do Partido dos Trabalhador.texto: Trade unionists, intellectuals and social movements found the PT at the Colégio Sion in São Paulo.

1981|Lojas do GOSP fundam o Grande Orien.titulo: GOSP lodges found the Grande Oriente Paulista
1981|Lojas do GOSP fundam o Grande Orien.texto: Lodges of the Grand Orient of São Paulo found the Grande Oriente Paulista (GOP), today one of the three Masonic Powers in the State.

1984|Comício das Diretas Já na Sé.titulo: Diretas Já rally at the Sé
1984|Comício das Diretas Já na Sé.texto: On the city’s anniversary, a crowd in Praça da Sé demands direct presidential elections.

1984|Rejeitada a Emenda Dante de Oliveir.texto: The amendment for direct elections fails to reach the necessary votes in the Chamber.

1985|Tancredo Neves eleito.texto: The Electoral College chooses the first civilian president since 1964.

1985|Morte de Tancredo; Sarney president.texto: Tancredo dies without taking office; Vice-President José Sarney, sworn in on 15 March, takes over permanently.

1986|Plano Cruzado.texto: Freezes prices and creates a new currency; the initial success gives way to new inflation.

1986|Acidente de Chernobyl.texto: An explosion at a nuclear plant in Soviet Ukraine causes the worst nuclear disaster in history.

1988|Constituição Cidadã.texto: The Constitution that restores rights and creates the SUS public health system is promulgated.

1988|Assassinato de Chico Mendes.texto: The rubber tapper and environmentalist is killed in Acre, with worldwide repercussions.

1989|Queda do Muro de Berlim.texto: The opening of the Wall symbolises the end of the Cold War; Germany reunifies in 1990.

1989|Primeira eleição direta desde 1960.texto: Fernando Collor defeats Lula in the December run-off.

1990|Plano Collor.texto: Freezes financial investments and savings to contain hyperinflation.

1991|Tratado de Assunção cria o Mercosul.texto: Brazil, Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay form a common market.

1991|Fim da União Soviética.texto: The USSR is dissolved, giving rise to 15 independent countries.

1992|Rio-92.texto: The UN conference on the environment brings heads of State together in Rio de Janeiro.

1992|Massacre do Carandiru.texto: A police intervention in the House of Detention leaves 111 prisoners dead.

1992|Impeachment de Collor.texto: Collor resigns during his trial in the Senate, which convicts him; Itamar Franco takes office.

1994|Morte de Ayrton Senna.texto: The three-time Formula 1 champion dies at Imola; his funeral in São Paulo moves the country.

1994|Mandela presidente.texto: Nelson Mandela becomes President of South Africa after the end of apartheid.

1994|Plano Real.texto: The real enters circulation and ends hyperinflation.

1994|Tetracampeonato nos EUA.titulo: Fourth world title in the USA
1994|Tetracampeonato nos EUA.texto: Brazil beats Italy on penalties and wins its fourth World Cup.

1995|Posse de Fernando Henrique Cardoso.texto: The former minister of the Real Plan becomes president; he would be re-elected in 1998.

1999|Criação do euro.texto: The common European currency comes into use in 11 countries.

2000|Lei de Responsabilidade Fiscal.texto: Sets spending and debt limits for governments.

2001|Atentados de 11 de Setembro.texto: Terrorist attacks destroy the Twin Towers in New York and strike the Pentagon.

2002|Pentacampeonato mundial.texto: In the final in Japan, Brazil beats Germany and wins its fifth World Cup.

2003|Posse de Lula.texto: The former ABC metalworker becomes president; he would be re-elected in 2006.

2003|Guerra do Iraque.texto: The USA and its allies invade Iraq and overthrow Saddam Hussein.

2006|Lei Cidade Limpa.texto: The city of São Paulo bans billboards and restricts advertising on façades.

2007|Descoberta do pré-sal.texto: Petrobras announces large oil reserves in deep waters.

2008|Crise financeira global.texto: The collapse of Lehman Brothers triggers the worst economic crisis since 1929.

2011|Posse de Dilma Rousseff.texto: The first woman to hold Brazil’s Presidency; she would be re-elected in 2014.

2013|Jornadas de Junho.texto: Protests against a bus fare increase in São Paulo spread across the country.

2014|Copa do Mundo no Brasil.texto: The country hosts the tournament for the second time; the opening match is in São Paulo.

2015|Rompimento da barragem de Mariana.texto: The disaster in Minas Gerais pollutes the Doce River all the way to the ocean.

2015|Acordo de Paris.texto: Almost every country commits to limiting global warming.

2016|Olimpíadas do Rio de Janeiro.texto: The first Olympic Games held in South America.

2016|Impeachment de Dilma Rousseff.texto: The Senate approves the president’s permanent removal; Michel Temer takes office.

2017|300 anos da maçonaria moderna.texto: Lodges around the world celebrate the tercentenary of the Grand Lodge of London, founded in 1717.

2018|O GOSP se desliga do Grande Oriente.titulo: GOSP leaves the Grand Orient of Brazil
2018|O GOSP se desliga do Grande Oriente.texto: In assembly, after contesting the GOB elections of August 2018, the Grand Orient of São Paulo approves its withdrawal from the federation by 82.5% of the votes and becomes an autonomous Masonic Power. The lodges that preferred to stay in the GOB reorganised as the GOB-SP.

2019|Posse de Jair Bolsonaro.texto: The president elected in 2018 takes office.

2019|Rompimento da barragem de Brumadinh.texto: The tragedy in Minas Gerais leaves 270 dead.

2020|OMS declara pandemia de covid-19.texto: The disease spreads around the world; in Brazil it would cause more than 700,000 deaths.

2021|Primeira vacina contra covid no Bra.texto: Nurse Mônica Calazans is vaccinated in São Paulo right after Anvisa’s approval.

2022|Rússia invade a Ucrânia.texto: The largest war in Europe since 1945 begins.

2022|Bicentenário da Independência.texto: The country celebrates 200 years of the Cry of Ipiranga; in São Paulo, the Ipiranga Museum reopens after restoration.

2023|Lula assume o terceiro mandato.texto: Elected in 2022, Lula returns to the Presidency.

2024|Enchentes no Rio Grande do Sul.titulo: Floods in Rio Grande do Sul
2024|Enchentes no Rio Grande do Sul.texto: Extreme rains in April and May hit most municipalities in the state.

2025|COP30 em Belém.texto: For the first time, the UN Climate Conference is held in the Brazilian Amazon.
